title: THE SAME REMEDY, THE SAME PLACE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"He shall dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle it before the LORD seven times in front of the curtain. He is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting. The rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tent of meeting."'" - Lev 4:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read these two verses beside verses 6 and 7 and you will find them nearly identical. Same sprinkling. Same seven times. Same horns of the incense altar. Same pouring at the base.

The sin of one priest and the sin of an entire nation received exactly the same remedy.

God does not have a stronger cleansing for bigger sins and a weaker one for smaller ones. There is one blood, applied one way, and it is sufficient in every case.

That should reach anyone who quietly believes their sin is a special case — too large, too repeated, too shameful for the ordinary provisions of grace. Scripture knows nothing of a sin that outsizes the remedy. Where sin increased, grace increased all the more (Rom 5:20). The blood of Jesus, God's Son, purifies us from all sin (1 Jn 1:7). All.

And it should also reach anyone who thinks their sin is too minor to require the cross. The community that sinned without even noticing still needed a bull, still needed blood, still needed the seven-fold sprinkling.

One remedy. Big enough for anything, necessary for everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe there is a sin in my life too big for God's forgiveness?
2. Do I treat any of my sins as too small to bring to the cross?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that there is one remedy and it is enough. Let me neither despair of Your grace nor take it lightly. Amen.
